clue.text: Care over count

parts.note: to reck is an old verb meaning to care or heed
on can mean over, as in a lid on (over) a box

explanation.surface: Someone tallies up how much they care before deciding.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to calculate or tally, the same sense as the verb count.

clue.text: Rose up in arms concerning handsome woman and daughter

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A rising is provoked over a beautiful woman and her child.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who revolt take up weapons against authority, which is what rising up in arms means.

clue.text: A turn needed to provide support for one side of farmer's vehicle

definitions.text: needed to provide support for one side of farmer's vehicle

explanation.surface: A farm vehicle's wheel described as a gymnastic move.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast's sideways handspring is named after the spoked wheel that carries one side of a farm cart.

clue.text: Following love and honour you must do as you are told

definitions.text: you must do as you are told

explanation.surface: The marriage vow reminds a bride or groom of their duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition points to the traditional marriage vow 'to love, honour and obey', where the answer comes after love and honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The vow's third verb follows love and honour, and complying with instructions is exactly doing as you are told.

clue.text: Kitchener's implement encourages many into a falsehood

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them

indicators.note: into means the word for many is placed inside the word for falsehood

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing for many

explanation.surface: A military man's tool urges many soldiers into telling an untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitchener' suggests the British field marshal, but here it simply means someone working in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A slotted flat utensil for lifting fried food is a classic kitchen tool.

clue.text: Fish to catch and deck. With a wreath of flowers?

definitions.text: deck. With a wreath of flowers

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
to land a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: An angler catches a fish and then decorates something with flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn with a wreath of blooms is the verb sense of a floral chain.

clue.text: Lear's lady-love was quite a barker.

definitions.text: Lear's lady-love was quite a barker.

parts.words: Lear's lady-love was quite a barker.
parts.note: in King Lear the king names his little dogs Tray, Blanch and a third whose name also means a beloved, and they bark at him

explanation.surface: King Lear's beloved turns out to be a noisy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady-love' suggests a woman Lear adored, but the barker is one of his dogs in Shakespeare's play (Act 3 Scene 6).
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, which is also the name of one of Lear's dogs.

clue.text: In a particle to be seen at… 6.55 the back of the head

parts.note: an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A tiny particle is spotted at the rear of someone's skull.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6.55' in the clue as held is stray print from the newspaper page and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: The inion is the bony bump on the skull at the back of the head, a point used in anatomy.

clue.text: Lead astray and foul net on the rocks

indicators.note: a fouled net is tangled, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a drink on the rocks is served with ice

explanation.surface: A fishing net tangled on rocks leads a boat off course.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or tempt someone into doing wrong is to lead them astray.

clue.text: Dexterous, according to the right in France

parts.note: French a, as in a la, means in the manner of or according to
droit is French for right

explanation.surface: Someone skilful acts according to French law.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilful with the hands, as dexterous means, is the sense of the borrowed French word for handy.

clue.text: One who serves drinks for a prison officer?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a barman could also be a jailer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as BAR TENDER: someone who tends the bars of a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub server pours drinks, and a jailer looks after (tends) cell bars.

clue.text: Be in bow of ship during outward passage

indicators.note: during means the letter from the ship sits within the word for a way out

parts.note: an exit is a way out

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a ship, so the front letter of ship is taken

explanation.surface: Someone stands in the bow of a ship as it heads out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to have being, the same as to live or have reality.

clue.text: Grass on a plot, giving some fine material

explanation.surface: A patch of turf on a plot yields some delicate fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Mown turf in a garden, and also a fine sheer linen or cotton cloth.

clue.text: Romantic about a French garment from ancient Italy

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the French article

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A dreamy person wraps themselves in a French garment from old Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans of antiquity wore a simple belted robe beneath the toga.

clue.text: Half-door to a small piece of land wherein to conspire

parts.note: a hatch is a small or half door
a plot is a small area of ground

explanation.surface: A gate leads to a small field where schemers meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Devising a secret scheme is what conspirators do together.

clue.text: Refined Eastern allowed to receive horse in retreat

indicators.note: to receive means the word for allowed takes the reversed horse inside it

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: in retreat means the word for horse goes backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A refined Easterner lets a horse in as it retreats.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and stylish in manner is what refined describes.

clue.text: Doctor on the border of a scoop

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A doctor stands at the edge of a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or bucket for scraping up mud from a riverbed acts as a large scoop.

clue.text: What Hamlet was? A hound?

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is asked whether he was a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet was a prince of Denmark, a notable man from there, and the big dog breed shares the name.

clue.text: Sticking together in company, man takes on lease

parts.note: he is a male pronoun, so stands for man
to rent is to lease

explanation.surface: A firm's employee takes on a property lease.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical consistency and holding together are both meanings of the adjective, as in a well-connected argument.

clue.text: French bell giving protection for gardeners

explanation.surface: A bell from France shelters plants.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word means bell; gardeners use a bell-shaped glass cover to shelter seedlings.

clue.text: Destroy the greatest number, although farthest away

parts.note: to end something is to destroy it
most is the greatest number

explanation.surface: Someone wipes out a great many even though they are remote.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative position at the extreme limit is the farthest point.

clue.text: A feature of submarine fish

explanation.surface: Something found on a submarine is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile fired from submarines, and the electric ray fish.

clue.text: Objective for sailor to attain

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to get is to attain

explanation.surface: A sailor sets out to reach a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal is something you shoot for, as with a mark.

clue.text: Put a roof on which little church?

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns
Ch is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone asks which small chapel needs roofing.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering a building with straw or reeds is roofing it.

clue.text: Drunk and thirsty stranded

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated
dry means thirsty

explanation.surface: Someone intoxicated yet still parched is left stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat left on the shore by the tide is stranded, the idiom for abandoned.

clue.text: This type of viewer can't see

definitions.text: This type of viewer can't see

parts.words: This type of viewer can't see
parts.note: viewer stands for an eye, and an artificial eye made of a transparent material is blind

explanation.surface: A remark about a spectator who is blind.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial eye is made from this material, so that kind of eye cannot see.

clue.text: A way you, archaically, may become an eyesore

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned street becomes an ugly sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Second-hand American edition

explanation.surface: A pre-owned copy of an American edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods already owned by someone else are not new.

clue.text: Drag along the first of, tee, teetotallers to a bar

indicators.note: the first of means only the opening letter of teetotallers is used

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: Abstainers are pulled along to a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'tee,' in the clue as held looks like a printing slip repeating the start of teetotallers.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something behind you along the ground is to drag it.

clue.text: Clear area that literally may have been left to be filled in later

definitions.text: may have been left to be filled in later

explanation.surface: A gap on a form waits to be completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbuilt land is a clear area, and a blank gap on a page is literally a space left open.

clue.text: Wait a second, a man is returning to the gallery

parts.note: he is a male pronoun, so stands for a man

indicators.note: returning means the little word is goes backwards

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend to pause while a man goes back to the gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause in indecision is to hold back briefly.

clue.text: Coming within a period that includes four Sundays

definitions.text: a period that includes four Sundays

explanation.surface: An arrival during the weeks before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an arrival, and the church season before Christmas covers four Sundays.
